title: Walks, circuits, trees, and spanning subgraphs
section: Graph Theory ▷ Paths, Trees, and Subgraphs
terms: walk; trail; path; closed walk; circuit; cycle; connected graph; connected component; forest; tree; subgraph; spanning subgraph; spanning tree.

exposition.text:
A walk follows adjacent vertices and may repeat vertices or edges. A trail repeats no edge; a
path repeats no vertex. A closed trail is a circuit, and a cycle is a closed path with only the
start/end vertex repeated. Terminology varies in the book, so inspect the intended repetition
rule. A graph is connected when every two vertices are joined by a path.
A connected component is a maximal connected subgraph. A subgraph uses subsets of the
original vertices and edges, with every retained edge keeping its endpoints. A forest has no
cycles; a connected forest is a tree. A forest with n vertices and c components has n − c edges.
A spanning subgraph retains all vertices, and a spanning tree is a spanning subgraph that is a
tree. Every finite connected graph has a spanning tree with n − 1 edges; a connected graph of
size m can therefore lose at most m − n + 1 edges while retaining connectedness.

question.text:
A connected graph has 17 vertices and 29 edges. What is the maximum number of edges that
can be deleted while keeping all vertices connected?
(A) 11 (B) 12 (C) 13 (D) 14 (E) 16

solution.text:
A spanning tree keeps 17 − 1 = 16 edges, so 29 − 16 = 13 can be deleted. Fewer than sixteen
remaining edges cannot connect seventeen vertices.

question.text:
A tree has four vertices of degree 3, two vertices of degree 4, and all remaining vertices have
degree 1. How many degree-one vertices are there?
(A) 6 (B) 8 (C) 10 (D) 12 (E) 14

solution.text:
If there are L leaves, the degree sum is L + 4(3) + 2(4) = L + 20. A tree on L + 6 vertices
has L + 5 edges, so L + 20 = 2(L + 5), giving L = 10.

question.text:
A forest has c connected components. A vertex of degree d and all of its incident edges are
deleted. How many connected components does the remaining forest have?
(A) c + d (B) c + d − 1 (C) c − d (D) c − d + 1 (E) c

solution.text:
Write the original vertex and edge counts as n, m, so m = n − c. After deletion they are n −
1, m − d, and the graph is still a forest. Its component count is (n − 1) − (m − d) = c + d − 1.
This also handles an isolated vertex (d = 0), whose deletion removes one component.

question.text:
In a simple graph, a, b, c, d, e are distinct vertices and the sequence a, b, c, a, d, e, a follows six
distinct edges. Under the terminology in this guide, the sequence is which of the following?
(A) A path but not a trail
(B) A cycle
(C) A circuit but not a cycle
(D) A walk but not a trail
(E) Neither a walk nor a circuit

solution.text:
No edge repeats, so the sequence is a trail. Its endpoints agree, making it a closed trail, or
circuit. The vertex a also occurs in the middle, so it is not a cycle. Closed walks, circuits,
and cycles impose different repetition restrictions.

question.text:
A graph has vertices 1, 2, 3, 4 and edges 12, 23, 34, 41, 13. How many spanning trees does it
have?
(A) 4 (B) 5 (C) 6 (D) 8 (E) 10

solution.text:
Without diagonal 13, a spanning tree is obtained by deleting one of the four cycle edges,
giving four. With the diagonal included, vertex 2 must attach by exactly one of 12, 23, and
vertex 4 by exactly one of 34, 41, giving 2 · 2 = 4. These cases exhaust the trees, for a total
of eight.
